subject: general
question: The marked price of a bookshelf is ₹3,100, which is 25% above the cost price. It is sold at a discount of 12% on the marked price. Find the profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Profit% can be calculated using the **successive percentage** formula when **Mark-up%** and **Discount%** are known.

Formula: **Profit% = M − D − (M × D) ÷ 100**, where M = Mark-up% and D = Discount%.

M = 25% and D = 12%.

Profit% = 25 − 12 − (25 × 12) ÷ 100 = 13 − (300 ÷ 100) = 13 − 3 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹3,100, **Mark-up** = 25% above CP, **Discount** = 12%.
Formulas: CP = MP × 100 ÷ (100 + Mark-up%) | SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100 | Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a65691b36a680d48fbd02170226b9b96da0481ae4ff288368b7eb163d3769421.png] 
⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = ₹100.
⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 25% of 100 = ₹125.
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 125 − 12% of 125 = 125 − (12 ÷ 100 × 125) = 125 − 15 = ₹110.
⇒ **Profit** = SP − CP = 110 − 100 = ₹10.
⇒ **Profit%** = (10 ÷ 100) × 100 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price**. SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Effective Change

When a value is increased by x% and then decreased by y%, the net change is given by (x − y − xy/100)%.
